answer: No ledge ticket is cut until a live bolt-pull is filmed. The applicant posts a 33-coin bond and sets a clerk-stamped 14 mm wedge anchor in joint 9 of licensed face C, whose resonance table is on-ledger. For 9 minutes they drape a numbered velvet sleeve over the lip and record the residual whisper after each 2.4 kN pull, every 10 s. Peers require frequency within 4 Hz of the table, the anchor lot in every still, and the sleeve cloth-lot hash matching the issued bolt. A plaster mock or borrowed wedge misses both checks and burns the stake, so each alias needs its own joint, sleeve, and pull.
